patient_information: A 21-year-old woman, 32 weeks pregnant with her first pregnancy, has no significant past medical history and is otherwise well.
history_of_present_illness: A 21-year-old pregnant woman, 32 weeks gestation, presented to clinic in The Gambia with a generalized, non-itchy rash that she had for 5 days. She reported no other symptoms and no significant past medical history.
physical_exam: She presented with a generalized macular rash involving the palms of both hands. Her mouth was normal, and there was no lymphadenopathy. She was not anaemic or jaundiced, and general examination was unremarkable.
differential_diagnosis: The generalized, non-itchy rash affecting the palms of the hands in this pregnant patient led to a clinical diagnosis of syphilis until proven otherwise, given its serious influence on pregnancy outcome.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was treated with a single intramuscular dose of benzathine penicillin (2.4 million units i.m.). She made an uneventful recovery and delivered a normal infant at term. Because she was treated after 28 weeks gestation, her infant was recommended to receive a course of treatment for congenital syphilis with IM procaine penicillin 50000 units/kg daily for 10-14 days.
final_diagnosis: The final diagnosis was secondary syphilis, clinically determined by a generalized, non-itchy macular rash involving the palms of both hands in a pregnant woman from The Gambia. The patient responded well to a single intramuscular dose of benzathine penicillin, leading to an uneventful recovery and the delivery of a normal infant at term, although the infant was prescribed treatment for congenital syphilis due to the timing of maternal treatment.
